comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Investigation: why uv locked pydantic-ai-slim 1.38.0, and what the fix must actually be.

FINDING 1 — uv.lock is NOT a repo artifact. It is gitignored (.gitignore:59-63: 'A uv.lock is thus a per-developer artifact'; core deps deliberately unpinned). AC2 ('uv.lock is regenerated') is therefore a local developer action, not a landable change. The landable change is pyproject.toml only.

FINDING 2 — the 1.38.0 pick is NOT a stale lock; it is a real cross-extra resolution conflict, reproducible from scratch. uv's universal resolution locks ALL extras jointly. Chain: [eval] -> inspect-ai 0.3.251 -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore (latest 2.25.1) pins boto3>=1.40.46,<1.40.62, while pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1.107 (pulled by the [bedrock] and [dev] extras) requires boto3>=1.42.63. Those are disjoint, so uv caps pydantic-ai-slim below 1.107 -> 1.38.0. 'uv lock --upgrade' today reproduces the same 1.38.0. A bare floor bump to >=1.107 makes the project UNRESOLVABLE under uv (verified: 'No solution found ... nava-rebar[bedrock], nava-rebar[eval] are incompatible').

FINDING 3 — pip is unaffected (installs one extra set at a time, and [dev]/[agents] never co-resolve with [eval]'s boto3 caps), which is why make install / the worktree venvs get the healthy 1.107.1 + 0.120.2 pair. Only uv-provisioned envs break.

FINDING 4 — verified fix: declare the extras conflict to uv. Adding
  [tool.uv]
  conflicts = [[{ extra = "eval" }, { extra = "bedrock" }], [{ extra = "eval" }, { extra = "dev" }]]
plus floor 'pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2' resolves cleanly to pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1 + anthropic 0.120.2 (tested in an isolated copy of the real pyproject). The minimal set suffices — eval+agents stays co-installable, matching the only real co-install (.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml installs '.[agents,eval]' via pip, which ignores [tool.uv] anyway). Nothing installs dev+eval together (Makefile uses '.[dev]').

REVISED APPROACH (nava-rebar is consumed externally from PyPI, so no speculative upper caps — floors only, per mainstream OSS practice):
1. pyproject [agents]: raise floor to pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2 (NOT <1.108). Drop the proposed explicit 'anthropic>=0.120,<0.121' pin — pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1's own [anthropic] extra already floors the SDK correctly (verified: fresh resolve picks 0.120.2); at most add a floor 'anthropic>=0.120' with no cap.
2. Add the [tool.uv] conflicts block above so uv-universal resolution stops downgrading pydantic-ai-slim to satisfy inspect-ai's boto3 cap.
3. The real regression guard is an import smoke test (AC3 as a CI test: 'from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel'), not the lock.
4. Developers with a broken local uv.lock: rm uv.lock && uv lock (or uv lock --upgrade) after the floor bump.

AC1/AC2 should be reworded accordingly: AC1 floors-only + conflicts block; AC2 becomes 'a from-scratch uv lock resolves pydantic-ai-slim>=1.107 + a compatible anthropic' rather than 'uv.lock is regenerated' (it is gitignored).

compiled_state.description:
# Go uv-canonical: matched pydantic-ai-slim + anthropic floors, [tool.uv] extras conflicts, committed uv.lock, and uv-locked install paths

## Problem

The direct Anthropic provider cannot import in uv-provisioned envs:
`pydantic_ai.models.anthropic` (in pydantic-ai-slim 1.38.0) does
`from anthropic.types.beta.beta_web_search_tool_20250305_param import UserLocation`, which does
not exist in anthropic 0.120.2. rebar's default config resolves `claude*` -> `_build_anthropic` ->
`AnthropicModel`, so local dev and the plan-review / code-review LLM gates break at import time.
The production review-bot is unaffected only because Bedrock does not import that module.

**Root cause (investigated, reproducible from scratch — NOT a stale lock):** uv's universal
resolution locks ALL extras jointly. `[eval]` -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore (latest
2.25.1) pins `boto3>=1.40.46,<1.40.62`, while `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1.107` (pulled by the
`[bedrock]` and `[dev]` extras) requires `boto3>=1.42.63`. Disjoint -> uv caps pydantic-ai-slim
below 1.107 -> 1.38.0. A bare floor bump to `>=1.107` makes the project UNRESOLVABLE under uv.
pip is unaffected (installs one extra set at a time; `[dev]`/`[agents]` never co-resolve with
`[eval]`'s boto3 caps), which is why `make install` envs get the healthy 1.107.1 + 0.120.2 pair.

**Verified fix for the resolution:** declare the extras conflict to uv —
`[tool.uv] conflicts = [[{extra="eval"},{extra="bedrock"}], [{extra="eval"},{extra="dev"}]]` —
plus floor `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2`. Tested against the real pyproject in
isolation: resolves cleanly to pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1 + anthropic 0.120.2. The minimal conflict
set keeps `eval`+`agents` co-installable, matching the only real co-install
(`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` installs `.[agents,eval]`). Nothing installs dev+eval
together.

## Decision (operator-approved 2026-08-02)

Adopt the pattern actively maintained OSS projects have converged on (pydantic, pydantic-ai
itself, Flask, MCP python-sdk, Ruff, openai-python all commit `uv.lock` and install from it in
CI): **go uv-canonical**. A committed lock is only a reproducibility guarantee if the install
paths honor it, so this ticket changes both together. Published metadata keeps loose floors
(nava-rebar is consumed externally from PyPI — no speculative upper caps, per mainstream
practice); the committed lock pins the repo's own envs.

## Scope

1. **`pyproject.toml`**
   - `[agents]`: raise floor to `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2` (floors only —
     drop the previously proposed `<1.108` / `anthropic<0.121` caps; pydantic-ai-slim 1.107's own
     `[anthropic]` extra already floors the SDK correctly, verified: fresh resolve picks 0.120.2).
   - Add `[tool.uv] conflicts` for `eval`⊥`bedrock` and `eval`⊥`dev` (the verified minimal set).
2. **Commit the lock**: remove `uv.lock` from `.gitignore` (rewrite the comment block at
   .gitignore:59-63), generate a fresh `uv.lock`, and verify it locks
   pydantic-ai-slim>=1.107 + a compatible anthropic.
3. **Install paths honor the lock**:
   - `Makefile` `install` -> uv-based locked install (`uv sync --locked` with the dev extra;
     keep the pre-commit hook wiring intact).
   - CI workflows -> `astral-sh/setup-uv` + `uv sync --locked` (respect the existing
     per-workflow extras, e.g. prompt-eval's `[agents,eval]`), plus a `uv lock --check` gate so
     a drifted lock fails CI.
   - `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` / `.opcert` -> locked uv install of
     `[agents,reviewbot]`.
   - (`Dockerfile.gerrit`'s unrelated pinned tool venv may stay pip.)
4. **`.github/dependabot.yml`**: add the `uv` block (the file's own comment anticipates exactly
   this: "Add a `uv` block only if a uv.lock is ever committed").
5. **Regression guard**: a CI-run import smoke test asserting
   `from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel` succeeds in the locked env with the
   agents extra.
6. **Docs**: `docs/local-dev-env.md` (uv becomes canonical, pip the alternative) and any
   bootstrap references in AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md that name `pip install -e '.[dev]'`.

Out of scope: provider selection, Bedrock/multi-provider changes, and any change to published
dependency metadata beyond the floors above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `pyproject.toml` `[agents]` floors `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2`
      (no one-minor upper caps anywhere in the change) and declares the `[tool.uv]` conflicts
      (`eval`⊥`bedrock`, `eval`⊥`dev`). No provider-selection changes.
- [ ] AC2: `uv.lock` is committed (removed from `.gitignore`), and a from-scratch
      `uv lock` reproduces it (`uv lock --check` passes); it locks pydantic-ai-slim>=1.107 with a
      compatible anthropic.
- [ ] AC3: `from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel` succeeds in a
      lock-synced venv, asserted by a CI-run smoke test.
- [ ] AC4: `make install`, CI test/lint/typecheck workflows, and the reviewbot/opcert images all
      install through the committed lock (`uv sync --locked` or equivalent `--frozen` uv install);
      CI fails when the lock drifts from pyproject.
- [ ] AC5: `.github/dependabot.yml` gains the `uv` block keeping the lock fresh.
- [ ] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the full test suite passes in the uv-locked CI.
- [ ] AC7: docs (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, bootstrap references) describe uv as canonical with pip
      as the equivalent alternative.

## Testing / Verification

From a fresh worktree venv provisioned via the new path:
- `uv sync --locked --extra dev && uv lock --check`
- `python -c "from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel; print('ok')"`
- `python -c "import anthropic, pydantic_ai; print(anthropic.__version__)"`
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, targeted reviewbot/container build if feasible locally.

## Risks / Notes

- The `eval`⊥`dev` conflict means `uv sync` cannot co-install those extras; verified no current
  consumer does (prompt-eval uses `[agents,eval]`; Makefile uses `[dev]`).
- The boto3 diamond heals itself when aiobotocore catches up to boto3>=1.42.63 upstream; the
  conflicts block can be revisited then but is harmless to keep.
- This may be large for one Gerrit change; if review friction demands, split along the seams
  (1+2 pyproject/lock, 3+4 install paths, 5+6 guard/docs) — each lands green independently with
  1+2 first.
